mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period with similar FEDFUNDS path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for lagged employment and unemployment variables (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 gains over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the identified demand acceleration (Granger causality rejected at 5% significance).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp drop in the ratio of orders to capacity (implied by industrial momentum) suggests softening supply constraints, which typically precedes S&P 500 upward surprises within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or down despite the supply easing signal (IC > 0.05 over the horizon).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns negative (i.e., rates are trending lower), the present value of future cash flows is boosted, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during the prior 60-day period with similar rate path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (implied by labor market dynamics) measured by a composite of employment and unemployment series (PAYEMS and UNRATE) triggers a risk-on sentiment shift in equities, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS + UNRATE cross into the upper quantile of their historical distribution (e.g., top 5%)
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive after controlling for the combined signal (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of higher inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% monthly for two months), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to rate hike expectations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar inflation path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply chain resilience (indicated by a sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sustained decline in inflation pressures (CPIAUCSL)) increases the expected earnings growth component of the S&P 500, yielding positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by > 5% while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.3% over 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for the supply resilience signal (Granger causality rejected at 5% significance).
